annotation_description: Jack-o'-Lantern is actually the best card to discard here for this deck's strategy. The Poxwalkers return from the graveyard whenever you cast a spell from anywhere other than your hand, so discarding a Poxwalkers would effectively not lose a card - it would set up the recursive engine. The reasoning given was completely wrong (calling Jack-o'-Lantern a '1/1 creature' when it's an artifact), but the actual choice of discarding Jack-o'-Lantern over Poxwalkers is a minor missed opportunity. Discarding a Poxwalkers would put it in the graveyard ready to be recurred, while Jack-o'-Lantern can at least be exiled from the graveyard for mana. However, the Poxwalkers synergy with the self-mill/combo plan makes discarding one of them clearly better.

Playing Verdant Catacombs before casting Once Upon a Time. If Once Upon a Time is still the first spell (free cast), it should be cast first to gain information before committing to a land drop. The top 5 cards might reveal a better land or change which creature to prioritize, affecting whether/how to use the fetchland.

Discarded Cabal Ritual instead of Poxwalkers. Poxwalkers has a recursion ability that triggers when casting spells from non-hand zones, meaning it's actually better in the graveyard for the Oops All Spells combo plan. Additionally, Cabal Ritual provides valuable mana acceleration redundancy for casting Balustrade Spy or Undercity Informer.

Cast Once Upon a Time before activating Verdant Catacombs. Fetching first would thin a land from the library, slightly improving the quality of the top 5 cards seen by Once Upon a Time. Activating a fetchland is not casting a spell, so Once Upon a Time would still be free afterward.

annotation_description: With only Verdant Catacombs as their sole land, taking Wight of the Reliquary over Misty Rainforest risks missing land drops. While they have two mana dorks in hand, they can only deploy one per turn, and if the dork gets removed they'd be stuck on one land. A fetchland would guarantee consistent mana development.

With only one Bayou available producing either B or G, casting Ignoble Hierarch (which produces B, R, or G but not the blue needed for anything) is reasonable for mana acceleration, but Thoughtseize might be more impactful here. The opponent has been casting Dark Rituals and Cabal Rituals, suggesting a combo deck. Thoughtseize would strip a key combo piece from their hand before they can go off, while Ignoble Hierarch just adds a mana dork that may not survive to be useful if the opponent combos next turn. However, Ignoble Hierarch does enable casting multiple spells next turn (like Thoughtseize + a 2-drop), so there's a reasonable argument for the mana dork line.

annotation_description: Exiling Cabal Ritual to pay for Unmask breaks the combo line of Dark Ritual → Cabal Ritual → Balustrade Spy (which would generate exactly 4 black mana needed for Spy). Without Cabal Ritual, Dark Ritual alone only produces 3 mana, which is insufficient for either combo creature to function (Balustrade Spy costs 4, Undercity Informer costs 3 but needs a creature + 1 mana to activate).

With Bayou and Ignoble Hierarch available (producing BG and B/R/G respectively), Libby has access to BG mana, which is exactly what Wight of the Reliquary costs. Wight is a 2/2 with vigilance that grows with creatures in the graveyard (currently 4 creature cards: Ignoble Hierarch, Grist the Hunger Tide which counts as a creature in graveyard, and potentially others depending on exact graveyard contents). With 4 creatures in graveyard (Ignoble Hierarch, Grist), Wight would be at least a 4/4. Additionally, Wight can sacrifice creatures to tutor lands, providing both board presence and utility. Birds of Paradise is a 0/1 mana dork that adds one mana of any color - useful but much less impactful than a large threat. Alternatively, Badgermole Cub costs 1G and provides a 2/2 body plus earthbend (animating a land as a creature with a +1/+1 counter) plus the mana-doubling ability with Ignoble Hierarch. However, Wight of the Reliquary is likely the strongest play here as it puts significant pressure on the board immediately as a large creature. Playing Birds of Paradise when you could deploy a meaningful threat is a tempo loss.

With 3 mana available (Forest, Ignoble Hierarch, Birds of Paradise), the player could cast both Thoughtseize (B) and Wight of the Reliquary (BG) this turn. Leading with Thoughtseize first is better sequencing - it reveals the opponent's hand, strips their best card, and provides information before committing to a threat. Casting Wight first means if the opponent has removal, you've lost information about whether to play differently.

Responding to Thoughtseize by casting Once Upon a Time gives the opponent more information and potentially a better card to take. The opponent sees whatever you find and can choose the best card from an expanded hand.

Balustrade Spy is the more dangerous combo piece - it mills the entire library on ETB for just {3}{B}, achievable with Dark Ritual + Elvish Spirit Guide. Undercity Informer requires both casting AND a separate activation with a creature sacrifice plus additional mana, making it harder to deploy in one turn. Taking Undercity Informer leaves the easier and more self-contained combo piece in hand.

Once Upon a Time costs {1}{G} when it's not the first spell of the game, and Kimi25 Libby has already cast multiple spells this game (Thoughtseize, Once Upon a Time previously, etc.). The 'cast without paying its mana cost' text says the annotation claims it was cast for free, but this is not the first spell of the game. If the game engine allowed this incorrectly, it's an engine issue. However, more importantly, casting Once Upon a Time before deploying creatures is questionable sequencing - Badgermole Cub would generate value by earthbending a land into a creature, and Wight of the Reliquary is already on board. With Bayou and Forest tapped and only Ignoble Hierarch and Birds of Paradise untapped for mana, spending {1}{G} on Once Upon a Time (if paid correctly) would consume the available mana that could cast Badgermole Cub instead. Badgermole Cub creates board presence and its earthbend ability makes a land into a creature (feeding Wight of the Reliquary's sacrifice ability). Additionally, Badgermole Cub's 'whenever you tap a creature for mana, add an additional {G}' would provide extra mana going forward. The Once Upon a Time is a speculative cantrip while Badgermole Cub develops the board meaningfully.

Narcomoeba is a key combo piece in this Balustrade Spy/mill-your-library strategy - when milled from library to graveyard, it comes into play for free, providing a body for Cabal Therapy flashback or other sacrifice effects. Discarding it to the graveyard removes it from the library where it would auto-trigger. Meanwhile, Poxwalkers actively wants to be in the graveyard since it returns to the battlefield whenever you cast a spell from anywhere other than your hand (which the combo involves).

Missed lethal damage. By playing Gaea's Cradle before combat, then casting Badgermole Cub (earthbending a land into a 1/1 haste creature) and second Wight of the Reliquary, all creatures could attack for 11 damage against opponent's empty board at 10 life.

Discarded Elvish Spirit Guide instead of Poxwalkers. Poxwalkers has 'Curse of the Walking Pox' - it returns from graveyard to battlefield whenever you cast a spell from anywhere other than your hand (e.g., Cabal Therapy flashback). Discarding Poxwalkers to graveyard would set up a free creature, which enables sacrifice fodder for Undercity Informer or Cabal Therapy flashback. ESG at least provides a mana of any color that could supplement a combo turn.
